To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we were able to identify the cortical spatiotemporally distributed network related to vestibular stimulation with natural acceleration profiles in a hexapod.
we have identified a cortical vestibular network that is activated during whole body accelerations.
we were able to identify robust VestEPs in response to naturalistic whole body translations, and that the CSv and the opercular–insular region are the main origin of these responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the cortical processing of vestibular information during active and passive body movements.
the investigation of the cortical processing of natural vestibular input.
the investigation of the human cortical vestibular network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vestibular evoking potentials are a robust and reliable measure to study the cortical processing of otolith stimulation in a naturalistic setting.
the vestibular system is a very important sensory system, which is involved in many functions of the body, including balance and orientation.
the vestibular system is not only a sensory organ, but a sensory motor system that is involved in the processing of the body in space and time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cingulate cortex is the main cortical area involved in the processing of vestibular signals.
the cingulate cortex is involved in the processing of otolith signals, and that this processing is modulated according to the acceleration intensity.
the vestibular organ is a key sensory system for the detection of egomotion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that the cortical spatiotemporally dynamic response to natural otolith stimuli can be measured by means of VestEPs.
we were able to identify the cortical vestibular response to natural stimulation for the three main acceleration directions.
we can now use VestEPs for the investigation of the mechanisms of inter-regional interactions in the natural context.
